minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to take charge of a found West Street Terrace cemetery and to buy Rainmaker licenses.
minutes.summary: The commission heard Carter lay out the legal routes (easement or eminent domain) for the found cemetery on private land. It then voted to take charge of it, aiming for a December 3 select board meeting. The Fish Street stone wall and the procurement rules were discussed, and the DPW director gave an update. The commission voted to buy Rainmaker software licenses over the DPW director's objection, and postponed the other agenda items.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted to take charge of a family cemetery plot found on private land on West Street Terrace, under state law, understood to be in perpetuity.
The commission voted to accept two Rainmaker software licenses and pay the total quoted, over the DPW director's objection.
The commission is aiming for a December 3 select board meeting to present the votes and ask for money for a survey, possibly from remaining ARPA funds.
On the Fish Street wall, the commission needs an actual price and written procurement advice, due for the January meeting.
The remaining agenda items were postponed to the next meeting, tentatively January 23.

why_it_matters: The town now has responsibility for a cemetery on land it does not own, and a survey and any easement or taking could fall on the select board, ARPA money, or local operating and trust fund dollars.
The Fish Street wall repair is not yet priced, so any cost would reach the operating budget or capital requests in the next fiscal year, and sale of lots would need a town meeting vote.
